items.title: Case IDs can escape the output folder or collide

findings.title: Case IDs can escape the output folder or collide
findings.explanation: A manifest case_id of '..' remains '..'; case_dir joins it to the selected output root, so saving a review or mask writes into its parent and can overwrite existing review.json or segmentation.seg.nrrd. Distinct IDs such as 'a/b' and 'ab' also map to the same folder, so one case can overwrite another case's corrections while their status entries remain distinct.
findings.suggestion: Reject '.' and '..', enforce resolved-path containment, and use a collision-resistant mapping or reject duplicate normalized case IDs before loading.

gpt.reason: TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbenchLib/storage.py:39-41: `safe = "".join(c for c in str(name) if c.isalnum() or c in ("_", "-", ".")).strip()`; lines 83-95: `return self.path(safe_name(cid))`. The input case ID is preserved by cases.py:19-20 and not validated by read_data_map at lines 88-98. Thus '..' selects the output root's parent, and a/b and ab collide. storage.py:268-271 writes the review there; TavrWorkbench.py:798-801 also saves a mask there. Existing files or another case's corrections can be overwritten.

gemini.reason: In TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbenchLib/storage.py:39-41, safe_name(name) strips non-[A-Za-z0-9_-.] characters rather than rejecting traversal tokens or normalizing separators, so safe_name('..') returns '..' and safe_name('a/b') == safe_name('ab') == 'ab'. Furthermore, storage.py:106 uses self.path(str(cid)) directly without safe_name. However, in normal use case_ids come from a user-selected local data_map.json, and OutputStore only writes fixed filenames (review.json, segmentation.seg.nrrd, etc.), so this is a minor path sanitization bug rather than a blocking exploit.

items.title: Dataset packaging can delete files outside the case directory

findings.title: Dataset packaging can delete files outside the case directory
findings.explanation: safe_name permits the case ID '..', and package constructs case_rel as cases/<ID>. For such a manifest, cleanup walks cases/.., i.e. the whole selected output directory, and removes files not in the new entry, including unrelated data. Even normal IDs cause untracked files in an existing case folder to be deleted without confirmation.
findings.suggestion: Reject dot components, verify resolved paths remain beneath a dedicated case directory, and remove only files recorded as generated by a previous run, with explicit confirmation or a non-destructive default.

gpt.reason: TavrWorkbench/tools/package_dataset.py:97-98: `return "".join(c for c in str(name) if c.isalnum() or c in "_-.") or "case"`; lines 144-152 derive `case_rel = f"cases/{safe_name(cid)}"` after requiring an existing image. Lines 124-131 walk that path and call `os.remove(full)` for every file not in the new entry. For '..', if the intermediate cases directory exists, the walk reaches the output root and recursively removes other files and case data. Ordinary case folders also have all unreferenced files removed, not just files tracked from a previous run.

gemini.reason: In TavrWorkbench/tools/package_dataset.py:97-98, safe_name('..') returns '..', and lines 121-135 (remove_stale_files) walk os.path.join(out_dir, 'cases', '..') (i.e. out_dir) and call os.remove(full) on any file not in keep. However, package_dataset.py is a standalone CLI helper script in tools/ (not imported or executed by the Slicer module) and requires a malformed case_id='..' in the user's input JSON to traverse out of cases/<id>, so it is a minor bug rather than a blocking safety issue.

items.title: TavrWorkbenchLib Python files are missing from MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS in CMakeLists.txt

findings.title: TavrWorkbenchLib Python files are missing from MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS in CMakeLists.txt
findings.explanation: `TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbench.py` imports 11 modules from the `TavrWorkbenchLib/` package (`annular_plane.py`, `annulus_pipeline.py`, `cases.py`, `constants.py`, `geometry.py`, `measurement_editor.py`, `rating_table.py`, `segmentation_editor.py`, `storage.py`, `valve_generator.py`, `valve_panel.py`, and `__init__.py`), but `TavrWorkbench/CMakeLists.txt` only lists `${MODULE_NAME}.py` in `MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS`. When built and packaged by the Slicer Extension build system, none of `TavrWorkbenchLib/*.py` will be installed, causing `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'TavrWorkbenchLib'` when Slicer attempts to load `TavrWorkbench`.
findings.suggestion: Add all `TavrWorkbenchLib/*.py` files (`TavrWorkbenchLib/__init__.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/annular_plane.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/annulus_pipeline.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/cases.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/constants.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/geometry.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/measurement_editor.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/rating_table.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/segmentation_editor.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/storage.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/valve_generator.py`, `TavrWorkbenchLib/valve_panel.py`) to `MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS` in `TavrWorkbench/CMakeLists.txt`.

findings.title: Packaged module omits its required helper package
findings.evidence:
set(MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS
  ${MODULE_NAME}.py
  )

set(MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES
  Resources/Icons/${MODULE_NAME}.png
  Resources/UI/${MODULE_NAME}.ui
  Resources/requirements.txt
findings.explanation: TavrWorkbench.py imports TavrWorkbenchLib.cases and other helpers at module import, but no helper files are listed for installation in this CMake file. A catalog-built package therefore lacks the package and cannot import the module, even though running from the source tree can work. This is a non-blocking extension packaging defect under the index admission policy.
findings.suggestion: Install all TavrWorkbenchLib Python files with their package directory preserved, and test loading the installed package in a clean Slicer.

gpt.reason: TavrWorkbench/CMakeLists.txt:5-7 lists only `  ${MODULE_NAME}.py`, and lines 16-20 pass just the listed scripts and resources to the Slicer macro. Root CMakeLists.txt:20-22 only adds that module directory; neither file installs the helper package separately. TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbench.py:30 imports `from TavrWorkbenchLib.cases import (case_id_of, has_contours, has_measurements, is_file, is_image_path,`. The built package therefore lacks required imports and the module cannot load. Broken loading is blocking under the severity rubric; this is distinct from the index policy's separate admission recommendation.

gemini.reason: TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbench.py:30-44 imports modules from TavrWorkbenchLib at module import time, while TavrWorkbench/CMakeLists.txt:5-7 only lists ${MODULE_NAME}.py in MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS. Because slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule only installs files listed in SCRIPTS and RESOURCES, the packaged extension will fail to load with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'TavrWorkbenchLib'. Under the review rubric, broken loading of the packaged extension is blocking.

items.title: macOS installer can delete an existing Slicer installation after a failed start

findings.title: macOS installer can delete an existing Slicer installation after a failed start
findings.evidence:
local broken="$SLICER_APP"
        rm -f "$MARKER"
        install_slicer fresh
        if [ "$SLICER_APP" = "$broken" ]; then
            # The standard location holds the broken copy itself: replace it with a fresh download
            rm -rf "$broken" 2>/dev/null || true
            [ ! -e "$broken" ] || die "Slicer at $broken cannot start. Drag it to the Trash, then run the command again."
            install_slicer fresh
findings.explanation: The installer may reuse an existing same-version Slicer application, not necessarily one it installed. If macOS terminates that process during configuration, the recovery path can recursively delete that application without asking, including any user modifications stored in it; a process termination does not prove the application is disposable.
findings.suggestion: Never automatically remove an existing Slicer application; install a separate copy or request explicit confirmation after identifying its ownership and backing it up.

gpt.reason: install/install_mac.sh:144-149 reuses an existing matching-version application, and lines 182-213 return 2 for a signal-terminated process with no result, not just a proven corrupt installation. Lines 224-231 contain `            rm -rf "$broken" 2>/dev/null || true` when the fresh lookup reuses the same path. This can delete a pre-existing Slicer application and its user modifications without consent after an unrelated termination.

gemini.reason: In install/install_mac.sh:148-150, if /Applications/Slicer.app already exists and matches the latest release version, the script sets SLICER_APP to it even if the user installed it independently. In configure_slicer (lines 220-231), if Slicer exits with status >= 128 before writing the result file (rc == 2), line 229 executes rm -rf "$broken" on that /Applications/Slicer.app and replaces it with a fresh download. While install/install_mac.sh is a standalone curl|bash helper script rather than part of the Slicer Extension Manager build, deleting an existing /Applications/Slicer.app without confirmation is a minor issue worth fixing.

items.title: Global VTK warning display disabled at module import time

findings.title: Global VTK warning display disabled at module import time
findings.evidence:
# Suppress VTK warnings globally to prevent console flooding and UI freezing
vtk.vtkObject.GlobalWarningDisplayOff()
findings.explanation: At module import time (when Slicer starts up and discovers scripted modules), `TavrWorkbench.py` disables VTK warning display globally across the entire Slicer process. This affects all users and all other modules even if the user never opens `TavrWorkbench`.
findings.suggestion: Remove `vtk.vtkObject.GlobalWarningDisplayOff()` at import time, or scope warning suppression locally around specific noisy operations and restore the previous `GlobalWarningDisplay` state in a `finally:` block.

findings.title: Import disables VTK warnings for the entire Slicer process
findings.evidence:
# Suppress VTK warnings globally to prevent console flooding and UI freezing
vtk.vtkObject.GlobalWarningDisplayOff()
findings.explanation: Once the module imports, VTK warnings from Slicer and other extensions are suppressed globally, including for users who never open TavrWorkbench. This hides diagnostic information unrelated to this module.
findings.suggestion: Remove the global toggle or narrowly handle the specific warnings in the operation that causes them.

gpt.reason: TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbench.py:46-47 has `vtk.vtkObject.GlobalWarningDisplayOff()` at top level, outside any module class or user action. When the module successfully imports, this switches off VTK warnings process-wide, hiding diagnostics from Slicer and other modules; the effect is contingent on the helper imports at lines 30-44 succeeding.

gemini.reason: TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbench.py:47 executes vtk.vtkObject.GlobalWarningDisplayOff() at module top level. When Slicer starts up and imports scripted modules during discovery, this globally disables VTK warning display across the entire Slicer session for all modules, even if the user never opens TavrWorkbench.

items.title: Navigating away discards unsaved mask edits without warning

findings.title: Navigating away discards unsaved mask edits without warning
findings.explanation: The leave check covers hinge and measurement edits but not segmentation edits. When a reviewer paints a mask and navigates without clicking Save Mask, loading the next case removes the current segmentation node, losing the changes without a prompt.
findings.suggestion: Track segmentation modifications and prompt to save, discard, or cancel navigation.

gpt.reason: TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbench.py:513-520 only checks `self.meas.hinges_moved()` and `self.meas.is_dirty()` before returning true; loadCase at lines 530-540 then loads the next case. Lines 553-562 remove nodes returned by `self.seg.release()`, including the segmentation node (segmentation_editor.py:99-111). saveCase at TavrWorkbench.py:715-760 does not save the mask; saveMask at lines 786-801 is separate. Navigating or using Save & Next without saving the mask can silently discard potentially extensive edits. This is non-blocking soundness feedback under the admission policy.

gemini.reason: TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbench.py:513-528 (_confirmLeaveCase) checks self.meas.hinges_moved() and self.meas.is_dirty(), and prompts to save contour/height edits via saveCase, which does not save the segmentation mask (saved separately via saveMask at line 786). Navigating to another case calls _loadCaseData -> _clearCaseNodes (lines 553-566), which removes the segmentation node from the MRML scene without warning if the user edited segments in the embedded Segment Editor without clicking Save Mask.

items.title: A failed image load is still marked as a loaded case

findings.title: A failed image load is still marked as a loaded case
findings.evidence:
self._cacheReview()      # keep in memory so Prev/Next doesn't lose ratings
        self.current_index = idx
        self._loadCaseData()
        self._case_loaded = True
        self._restoreReview(idx)
findings.explanation: _loadCaseData returns False when the image cannot be loaded, but this caller ignores the result and sets _case_loaded to True. The interface can then show the failed case as loaded and permit review actions despite the missing volume.
findings.suggestion: Check the return value and leave the case unloaded, with review actions disabled, on failure.

items.title: Documentation describes workflows absent from the current module

findings.title: Documentation describes workflows absent from the current module
findings.evidence:
The Input panel offers two ways to load a dataset. Choose one using the Directory or JSON Manifest option.

### Directory Mode

Select a folder that contains your volumes in .nii, .nii.gz or .nrrd format. The module finds the cases in one of three ways.

1. Automatic pairing: each volume is matched with a mask that shares its name and ends with _mask, for example case01.nii.gz and case01_mask.nii.gz.
findings.explanation: The inspected module sets up a JSON map selector and calls read_data_map; it does not implement the documented directory input. The README also describes a three-option rating scheme while the current interface uses Approve and Flag, which can mislead new reviewers.
findings.suggestion: Update the tutorial and output descriptions to match the current UI, and provide a representative sample manifest and clinical-use limitations.

items.title: Extension uses CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license (NonCommercial, NoDerivatives)

findings.title: Extension uses CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license (NonCommercial, NoDerivatives)
findings.evidence: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International Public License
findings.explanation: The repository is licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (`LICENSE.md` and `LICENSE.txt`), which permits reproduction and sharing of the unmodified material for non-commercial purposes only and prohibits sharing adapted material. While this permits verbatim distribution by the Extensions Index, users should be aware of the non-commercial and no-derivatives restrictions, and a standard open-source software license (such as BSD, MIT, or Apache 2.0) is generally recommended for code repositories.
findings.suggestion: Consider whether an open-source software license (or at least noting the non-commercial restriction in `README.md`) is appropriate for your intended users.

items.title: License limits redistribution and commercial use

findings.title: License limits redistribution and commercial use
findings.evidence:
the Licensed Rights in the Licensed Material to:
             A. reproduce and Share the Licensed Material, in whole or in part,
                for NonCommercial purposes only; and
             B. produce and reproduce, but not Share, Adapted Material for
                NonCommercial purposes only.
findings.explanation: The license permits noncommercial sharing of the unadapted material, but users cannot rely on it for commercial use or to distribute adaptations. This is a material restriction for prospective users, not by itself evidence that an unmodified catalog package cannot be distributed.
findings.suggestion: Make the restrictions prominent in extension metadata and documentation, and retain required attribution in distributed packages.

items.title: Module category set to Examples, placeholder help URL, and outdated README

findings.title: Module category set to Examples, placeholder help URL, and outdated README
findings.evidence: self.parent.title = _("TavrWorkbench") self.parent.categories = [translate("qSlicerAbstractCoreModule", "Examples")] self.parent.dependencies = ["Segmentations", "SegmentStatistics", "Markups"] self.parent.contributors = ["Mohammed Khubaib (Saeed Lab: Florida International University)"] self.parent.helpText = _(""" A 3D Slicer extension for fast, structured review of TAVR CT segmentations and measurements. Switch between Segmentation review (approve / flag / edit masks) and Measurements review (correct annulus, SOV and STJ contours with live metrics, view heights) on the same case list. Shortcuts: Shift+A approve, Shift+F flag (current mode), Shift+Return save & next. See more information in module documentation. """)
findings.explanation: In `TavrWorkbench.py`, `self.parent.categories` is set to `"Examples"` (whereas `CMakeLists.txt` and the catalog entry use `"Segmentation"`), and `self.parent.helpText` still contains the template placeholder URL `https://github.com/organization/projectname#TavrWorkbench`. Additionally, `README.md` describes an older UI (e.g., "Directory Mode", "Centerline Slicing", and "The module installs pandas, numpy and SimpleITK automatically") that does not match the current implementation.
findings.suggestion: Set `self.parent.categories = ["Segmentation"]`, update the documentation link in `helpText` to `https://github.com/pcdslab/TavrWorkbench`, and update `README.md` to reflect the current 4-tab workflow.

dispute_items.title: Navigating away discards unsaved mask edits without warning

findings.title: Navigating away discards unsaved mask edits without warning
findings.explanation: The leave check covers hinge and measurement edits but not segmentation edits. When a reviewer paints a mask and navigates without clicking Save Mask, loading the next case removes the current segmentation node, losing the changes without a prompt.
findings.suggestion: Track segmentation modifications and prompt to save, discard, or cancel navigation.

gpt.reason: TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbench.py:513-520 only checks `self.meas.hinges_moved()` and `self.meas.is_dirty()` before returning true; loadCase at lines 530-540 then loads the next case. Lines 553-562 remove nodes returned by `self.seg.release()`, including the segmentation node (segmentation_editor.py:99-111). saveCase at TavrWorkbench.py:715-760 does not save the mask; saveMask at lines 786-801 is separate. Navigating or using Save & Next without saving the mask can silently discard potentially extensive edits. This is non-blocking soundness feedback under the admission policy.

gemini.reason: TavrWorkbench/TavrWorkbench.py:513-528 (_confirmLeaveCase) checks self.meas.hinges_moved() and self.meas.is_dirty(), and prompts to save contour/height edits via saveCase, which does not save the segmentation mask (saved separately via saveMask at line 786). Navigating to another case calls _loadCaseData -> _clearCaseNodes (lines 553-566), which removes the segmentation node from the MRML scene without warning if the user edited segments in the embedded Segment Editor without clicking Save Mask.
